body.statement: Proposition 2. If \(0\le s\le s'\le J\), then \(\Theta_{J,s}\subseteq\Theta_{J,s'}\) and \(R^*(J,s)\le R^*(J,s')\). At \(s=0\), \(R^*(J,0)=0\) and \(\mathcal Q^*(J,0)=\{q^{\mathrm{pair}}\}\). At \(s=J\), \(R^*(J,J)=r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}\), and \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\in\mathcal Q^*(J,J)\) with the nonlinear posterior-mean rule from the unrestricted binary experiment.
body.justification: The endpoints are mandatory reductions: perfect pair agreement makes paired assignment exact, while a vacuous budget recovers the published unrestricted problem.
body.gap: Bai2022MatchedPairs and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes motivate opposite endpoint prescriptions under different information classes; this proposition embeds both endpoints in one fixed-population model.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain a monotone worst-case-risk sensitivity curve in \(s\), with familiar paired and Bernoulli procedures anchoring its two endpoints; the optimal face itself is recomputed at each sensitivity value.
